## Purpose

Each `mustard` subcommand owns a small `*Options` struct that names the flags it accepts, and nothing else. The struct is deliberately argv-blind: `clap` lives one layer up in `apps/cli/src/cli.rs`, where the `Commands` enum carries the `#[arg(...)]` attributes and `dispatch` builds the struct literal by hand. That split is what lets the command functions be a reusable library — the dashboard's Tauri crate depends on `mustard-cli` and drives it that way in `apps/dashboard/src-tauri/tests/mustard_cli_test.rs`, calling `init_with_templates(&project, &templates, &InitOptions { yes: true, ..InitOptions::default() })` exactly as the in-file unit tests do, with no process `argv` in sight. Keeping the struct plain also keeps the flag surface reviewable in one glance: at most three fields, one `///` doc each, one derive attribute. A new subcommand that skips the struct and passes loose booleans breaks both callers, because the signature stops being stable when a flag is added.

## Convention

Folder: apps/cli/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 4

Beyond the census facts, what the files themselves show:

- **Name and place.** The struct is the subcommand in UpperCamelCase plus the `Options` suffix (`AddOptions`, `ConfigOptions`, `InitOptions`, `InstallNerdFontOptions`), declared in the same module as its command function, immediately after the `use` block and before any private helper type.
- **Derive set.** All four carry exactly `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]` — no `clap` derive, no `serde` attributes. The derived `Default` is what tests rely on to build a partial literal and fill the rest with the struct-update shorthand.
- **Doc habits.** All four are introduced by the same one-line doc comment, ``/// Flags accepted by `mustard <subcommand>`.``, and every field carries its own `///` doc stating the flag's effect ("Overwrite files that already exist in `.claude/`.", "Accept defaults without prompting.") — one line, or two when the value needs its domain named (`font` points at `DEFAULT_FONT` and `KNOWN_FONTS`).
- **Fields.** Every field is `pub` and a plain owned type — `bool` for a switch, `Option<String>` for a valued flag. Defaults are resolved inside the command function (`options.font.as_deref().unwrap_or(DEFAULT_FONT)`), never encoded as a non-`Default` field type.
- **Entry signature.** The command function takes the target path first and the options last, borrowed: `pub fn config(project_path: &Path, options: &ConfigOptions) -> Result<()>`. Anything extra lands in the middle, never after the options — `add` slots its positional there (`cwd: &Path, template_spec: &str, options: &AddOptions`), and so does the second entry point `init_with_templates(project_path: &Path, templates_dir: &Path, options: &InitOptions)`. The path parameter stays in the signature even where the body ignores it (`install_nerd_font(_project_path: &Path, options: &InstallNerdFontOptions)`), so every arm of `dispatch` reads alike. The return is `anyhow::Result<()>` in all four.
- **Test placement.** Unit tests sit in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the same file and construct the struct directly — `&AddOptions::default()` in `add.rs`, a full literal in `install_nerd_font.rs`. `config.rs` is the one file with no test module: it is a two-line wrapper, and what it forwards to is covered by `git_flow.rs`'s own `mod tests`.
- **The one test that must leave the process.** `apps/cli/tests/private_init.rs` runs the built binary as a child (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_mustard")`) and reads its exit code, for the two reasons its header states. First, `init_with_templates` opens with the `probe_rtk()` hard gate, whose `std::process::exit(1)` is neutralised only by `cfg!(test)` — and that is FALSE in an integration test, which links the crate as an ordinary dependency, so an in-process call would take the whole test binary down on a runner without RTK; as a child, that exit code becomes an assertion instead of a casualty. Second, the behaviour under test fires on a condition no flag carries (the project having a `github.com` origin), so only a real install against a real repository proves it; the tool `--version` probes are answered by a PATH shim dir instead of the runner's tools. Reach for `tests/` only under that shape — a `process::exit` gate, or a precondition no field of the options can express. Everything a borrowed `&*Options` can drive belongs in the in-file `mod tests`. (The subproject's other integration file, `apps/cli/tests/template_budget.rs`, gates the `.md` template corpus, not a command.)
- **One sibling deviates, in two places only:** `install_grammars.rs` names its struct `InstallGrammarsArgs`, and its entry point is `pub fn run(args: InstallGrammarsArgs) -> Result<()>` — taken by value, with no leading `&Path` (the root arrives as `project_root: Option<PathBuf>` and falls back to `std::env::current_dir()` inside). Everything else there already follows this mold: the same `#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]`, the same ``/// Flags accepted by `mustard install-grammars`.`` intro line, a `pub` owned field with its own `///` doc, and no `clap` attribute. Take the name and the signature from the four `*Options` files; that file is not a second convention.

## How to apply

A new subcommand gets its own file in `apps/cli/src/commands/`, registered with a `pub mod` line in `apps/cli/src/commands/mod.rs`. Open the file with a `//!` module doc that explains what the command does and why (the existing modules use it to record the reasoning, not just the summary), then declare the `*Options` struct with the derive set and per-field doc lines above, then the `pub fn` entry point taking `&Path` first and `&YourOptions` last.

Wire it in `apps/cli/src/cli.rs`: add a variant to `Commands` whose fields mirror the struct field-for-field with `#[arg(...)]` attributes (`#[arg(short, long)]` for `force`, `#[arg(short = 'y', long)]` for `yes`, `#[arg(long = "dry-run")]` for `dry_run`), import the struct beside its module (`use crate::commands::foo::{self, FooOptions};`), and add the `match` arm that builds the literal and calls the function.

Must not: put `clap` or `serde` attributes on the `*Options` struct; take it by value; make a field private or add a constructor when a public field would do; drop the `Default` derive; read `std::env::args` from inside `commands/`. Per the subproject guards, no `unwrap`/`expect` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — surface failures as `anyhow` errors with `.with_context(...)`.

## Examples

- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/config.rs — the minimal form: one `yes: bool` field and a two-line entry function that forwards `!options.yes` as `interactive`.
- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/init.rs — three flags (`force`, `yes`, `dry_run`), each consumed at a distinct decision point (`decide_existing_action`, the dry-run early return), plus the split entry point (`init` / `init_with_templates`) that keeps environment resolution out of the logic.
- Ref: apps/cli/src/commands/install_nerd_font.rs — the valued-flag shape: `font: Option<String>` with the default resolved in the function body, and tests that build the struct literal directly.
